due.in_days: {0} due today|{1} 1 day left|[2,*] :count days left

requests.title: GDPR requests
requests.intro: Access, export, erasure, rectification, objection and restriction. Answer within one month of receipt, extendable once by two months (Art. 12(3) GDPR).
requests.caption: GDPR requests by due date
requests.empty_body: Record requests that come by e‑mail, letter or support here. Exports and deletions from the app are listed below.
requests.self_body: Data exports and account deletions that members started themselves in the settings. For the overview only, no further steps.
requests.self_empty: No exports or deletions from the app yet.

create.title: Record request
create.body: The deadline starts on receipt and ends one month later.
create.member_unknown: There is no member with this username.
create.name: Name
create.received_hint: Leave empty for today. At most one year back.
create.details_hint: What the person asks for, up to 5,000 characters.

request.error: The request could not be loaded
request.no_address: No e‑mail address known: replies cannot be sent.
request.extend_hint: Possible once, before the first deadline ends. Then send the reply “Extension”.
request.reply_body: The template names the DS number and the deadline. Only the fact that the reply was sent is stored, not its text.
request.detail_hint: Optional, up to 2,000 characters, below the template text.

template_about.received: Confirms receipt and names the deadline.
template_about.identity: Asks for proof that the request comes from the person themselves.
template_about.extension: Announces the two-month extension with its reason. Only after “Extend deadline”.
template_about.completed: Says that the request is done.
template_about.rejected: Gives the grounds and the way to the supervisory authority and the court. Only after “Reject”.

request.complete_body: Closing needs evidence: a note, a file or both. A refusal needs its grounds as a note.
request.note_hint: What was done and when, 10 to 5,000 characters.
request.file_hint: PDF, image, text or ZIP, up to 10 MB. Stored privately; only team members with the privacy permission download it.
request.final: This request is closed. It stays with its evidence as long as set under “Retention”.
request.view_only: You can view the request; team members with “Process GDPR requests” work on it.

errors.evidence: Add evidence: a note or a file.
errors.reject_note: A refusal needs its grounds as a note (10 to 5,000 characters).

request.no_member_address: The account has no reachable e‑mail address: replies cannot be sent.

extend.title: Extend the deadline by two months
extend.body: New deadline: :date. Possible only once. Then send the reply “Extension of the deadline” with the reason.

export.title: Send the data export to the member
export.body: The member gets their data export by e‑mail as in the app, with a link that works for 7 days. The team does not see the file. Check the identity first.

erasure.title: Ask for the account’s erasure
erasure.body: After a second person approves, the account closes at once and is deleted for good within 30 days, as with a deletion in the app. Then close the request with evidence.

retention.title: Retention
retention.intro: How long data stays before the daily clean-up jobs delete it. Every value lies between the legal or technical minimum and what the privacy policy promises.
retention.caption: Retention periods
retention.error: The periods could not be loaded
retention.fixed_body: These periods are set by technology, law or the hosting and cannot be changed here.
retention.confirm_body: The new periods apply from the next run of the clean-up jobs. The change goes into the audit log with its reason.
retention.view_only: You can view the periods; team members with “Change retention periods” change them.

accounts_hard_delete_days.label: Deleted accounts
accounts_hard_delete_days.note: Then deleted for good. At least 7 days, so long the data export stays available after the deletion request; at most 30 days as the privacy policy says.

deleted_vehicles_days.label: Deleted vehicles
deleted_vehicles_days.note: Data and photos of deleted vehicles. At most 30 days as the privacy policy says.

deleted_media_days.label: Deleted photos
deleted_media_days.note: Photos members deleted. At most 30 days as the privacy policy says.

unverified_accounts_days.label: Unconfirmed accounts
unverified_accounts_days.note: Accounts without a confirmed e‑mail address. At least 2 days so the confirmation link stays usable; at most 7 days.

known_devices_months.label: Known devices
known_devices_months.note: For the notice about a sign-in from a new device. At most 12 months.

support_tickets_months.label: Support tickets
support_tickets_months.note: Closed tickets. At least 6 months for follow-up questions, at most 24 months as the privacy policy says.

audit_access_months.label: IP addresses in the audit log
audit_access_months.note: IP address and browser of team members for audit events, outside the hash chain. 6 to 12 months.

privacy_requests_months.label: GDPR requests
privacy_requests_months.note: Closed requests with evidence. At least 36 months: accountability (Art. 5(2) GDPR) for the 3-year limitation period (§ 195 BGB).

messages_of_deleted_members.label: Messages of deleted members
messages_of_deleted_members.note: The other side keeps its copy; the sender appears anonymous.

audit_events.label: Audit events
audit_events.note: With the daily exports of the hash chain.

audit_archive.label: Audit log archive
audit_archive.note: Then an archived export, up to this age.

moderation_cases.label: Moderation cases
moderation_cases.note: For legal defence. The period is still with legal counsel.

qr_scans.label: QR scans
qr_scans.note: Only counted views per day, no personal data.

flash.created: Request created. The deadline is running.
flash.extended: Deadline extended. Now send the reply “Extension of the deadline”.
flash.export_sent: The export is being built and sent to the member by e‑mail.
flash.rejected: Request rejected. Now send the reply “Refusal”.
